note: The reported symptom is the internal-error text `llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!` produced by an ordinary compile of repro.hlsl, per the issue body. Measured on the ground-truth main-debug build, the same underlying bad `llvm::cast` instead trips as a trapped LLVM assert, exit 0xE0000001 (STATUS_LLVM_ASSERT), because a Debug build has assertions compiled in where the reporter's build did not -- this is the Debug/Release signature split SKILL.md documents (a bad cast throws hlsl::Exception(DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR, ...), which a Release/NDEBUG build reports as plain E_FAIL with the llvm::cast text, while Debug traps first). `internal_failure` covers both signatures of the same defect: the exit-code path (0xE0000001 is in INTERNAL_STATUS) catches the Debug ground truth, and the text-marker fallback (`(?:llvm::)?cast<[^>]*>\(\) argument`) would catch a Release build reporting plain E_FAIL with the llvm::cast text, matching the reporter's own quoted output. CONTROL: control-initialized.hlsl (identical shader, but X is initialized to 0 before use) must compile cleanly and must NOT match -- see variant-initialized-*.txt. That proves the predicate fires on the uninitialized-index defect and not merely on structured-buffer array-member codegen in general.
